name: Amaranth Purple
lede: Amaranth Purple is a saturated purplish red, closer in the color graph to several named reds than to any true purple.

sections.title: A name in the library
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 filed this name under block 256, deep purplish red, despite the word "purple" in its name [1]. Wikipedia's entry on the color cites Maerz and Paul as an earlier source, but the library's own dictionary record keeps no first date [1]. In the color graph, the closest neighbors are all reds: [[raspberry]] at 2.7 units, [[big-dip-o-ruby]] close behind at 3.8, and [[berry-red]] and [[berry-red]] tied just beyond that at 4.1 [2].

Munsell notation reads 0.8R 3.9/11.8, a dark, highly saturated red-leaning hue [1]. The hex #AB274F is a screen approximation; no plate or swatch number survives in the library record consulted here [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 4 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [3]. The earliest is Jusepe de Ribera's *Saint John the Baptist in the Desert* (1650); the others date from about 1900 on, including Ernst Ludwig Kirchner's *Two Girls under an Umbrella* (1910) and two Indian paintings in the Cleveland Museum's collection [3]. Among this small set, Indian paintings and the 1900s decade both stand out well above the archive's base rate [3]. The sample is small enough that this is a pattern worth noting, not a conclusion [3].
